trust_decision.summary: lsup.sh, which runs as root, trusts work and lock paths that a less-privileged user can create or replace: the server-user-owned SERVER_ROOT/autoupdate work dir (tarball extraction, ols.conf write, ./install.sh exec), fixed /tmp names (lock, tmprelease, testpid). It also installs an unverified download (curl -k, no checksum). The fix moves all of this into a root-created 0700 admin/update dir and adds a check of VERSION and SHA-256.

landing_point.why: The summary names the lsup.sh auto-update. TEMPPATH=autoupdate plus cd plus the ols.tgz check-then-remove is the obvious TOCTOU spot, with the /tmp/olsupdatingflag lock at line 450-464.

fix_sites.entry_point: lsup.sh (every invocation; DLCMD curl -k / wget follows redirects)

fix_sites.module_kind: shell script, lock + work dir selection
shell script, download without integrity check

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix touches only dist/admin/misc/lsup.sh (fix.diff:97-430). The unsafe ownership of autoupdate/ comes from C++ and the installer (src/main/httpserver.cpp:3998, src/main/httpserver.cpp:4133, dist/functions.sh:991), which the fix leaves unchanged and bypasses by moving the work dir.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The /tmp/lshttpd and /tmp/shm paths (lsup.sh:262, 306-309, 554-557) belong to the server's runtime tmp dir and the debug/core tooling, not to the update download, so a solver can call them a neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The server worker (non-root) must still be able to write autoupdate/release and releasecb, which the version check and the WebAdmin 'new version' banner read, and lsup.sh still reads autoupdate/release for the default VERSION. An over-broad fix that makes autoupdate/ root-only or stops lsup.sh reading release breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: pre-existing work dir path is a symlink or not a directory (fix.diff:120-123)
VERSION string with non-digit, leading or trailing dot, or '..' (fix.diff:253-258)
downloader variants wget / curl / fetch, with https-only and redirects (fix.diff:137,146,152)
package too small vs checksum mismatch vs checksum download failure (fix.diff:272-312)
Linux prebuilt SRCDIR vs non-Linux source SRCDIR, either one a symlink (fix.diff:382-392)

O7_producer.where: src/main/httpserver.cpp:3994-3998 and src/main/httpserver.cpp:4133 (testAndFixDirs at src/main/httpserver.cpp:3377-3410, during server config setup as root, chowns autoupdate/ to the worker uid). Installer: dist/functions.sh:919, dist/functions.sh:991

O8_uncovered_routes.route: upgrade path, run as root, moves /tmp/lshttpd/bak_core to the fixed name /tmp/lshttpdcore
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: core-file housekeeping, not part of the download/install

O8_uncovered_routes.route: -t test: check-then-mkdir /tmp/lshttpd/bak_core, then mv core files into it as root
-c clean, run as root: rm -rf on the worker-owned autoupdate/* (no longer the work dir after the fix)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: after the fix autoupdate/ only holds release files; rm -rf does not follow symlinks

O8_uncovered_routes.route: stopService kill -9 on a pid read from /tmp/lshttpd/lshttpd.pid
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: pid file belongs to the server's runtime contract, not the updater

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A C++ startup step that pre-creates or chowns admin/update for the worker uid, as it already does for autoupdate/ and cgid/.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same block already pre-creates and chowns sibling dirs 'because user can change user/group setting'; adding the new dir there looks natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The installer list of util_mkdir/chown $DIR_OWN dirs gains admin/update, or lsup.sh state is placed in a $DIR_OWN dir.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The installer bulk-chowns runtime dirs to the server user, and maintainers append dirs to these lists.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The gdb core dump writes or reads a temp command file in /tmp before ${LSWSHOME}/corefile.txt.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The script already writes ps output to /tmp/testpid in the same style (lsup.sh:204).

O9_family: TOCTOU / insecure temp and work directory in a privileged updater script (CWE-367, with CWE-377/CWE-494 aspects)

O10_build.language: Shell (POSIX sh); the surrounding server is C/C++
O10_build.toolchain: /bin/sh plus coreutils, tar, sha256sum, wget or curl; the script needs no build. C++ server: cmake/build.sh (not needed for this script)
services: HTTPS download server (stubbable by a fake wget/curl on PATH)
O10_build.project_tests: None for lsup.sh. The repo test/ dir has no updater tests (test/serverroot/bin/lshttpd.sh only references the pid file).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the /tmp/olsupdatingflag check-then-touch with mkdir-as-lock (or mktemp) and keep extracting/running install.sh inside the worker-owned SERVER_ROOT/autoupdate.

out_of_scope_notes: The first fix commit also adds blocking of PATH/LS_/LD_/LSAPI_ env names in RequestVars::setEnv (fix.diff:21-41, src/http/requestvars.cpp:1410). This is a separate env-injection issue, not this advisory.
lshttpdmain.cpp crash handler runs ::system mkdir/mv/rm on DEFAULT_TMP_DIR/bak_core (src/main/lshttpdmain.cpp:230-239). Same /tmp core pattern, but in C++ and not part of lsup.sh.
testbeta.sh and update.sh are listed in dist/functions.sh:1018 but do not exist in the tree; the testbeta.sh call is dead code under '#if 1' (src/main/lshttpdmain.cpp:189-225).
